title: Salted Maple Banana Bread
description: An enormous, supremely moist banana bread from @theselena_v, made with browned butter, brown sugar, ripe bananas, buttermilk, and molasses, finished straight from the oven with Grade A maple syrup and a sprinkle of flaky salt. Makes multiple XL loaves.
yield: Multiple XL loaves (recipe makes an obscene amount)

ingredients.note: Transcript says approximately 12 bananas; caption amount 1190 g is authoritative. Use very ripe bananas.
Author notes they may increase salt next time to further bring out banana flavor.
Caption says "a full half cup per loaf" per transcript; caption instructs to splurge on the best quality. Exact total quantity depends on number of loaves.
Transcript says "malt and salt" which is interpreted as flaky/maldon salt; qty not given in caption or transcript.

steps.title: Beat butter and sugars
steps.text: In the largest bowl or stand mixer you have, beat {i01} with {i02} and {i03} until light and fluffy.

steps.title: Add mashed bananas
steps.text: Add {i04} to the butter-sugar mixture and mix in. The batter will look severely split and curdled — this is normal. Trust the process.

steps.title: Add eggs, molasses, and vanilla
steps.text: Add {i05} one at a time, then mix in {i06} and {i07} until combined.

steps.title: Whisk dry ingredients
steps.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together {i08}, {i09}, and {i10} until evenly combined.

steps.title: Fold dry into wet
steps.text: Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and fold together until just incorporated. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Stream in buttermilk
steps.text: Add {i11} a half cup at a time, folding gently after each addition until the batter reaches a smooth, cohesive texture.

steps.title: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.text: Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease XL loaf pans (Pullman pans work well but any XL loaf pan is fine). Divide batter evenly among the pans.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 325°F. Begin checking the loaves around 90 minutes (transcript says the baker starts checking at 1 hour 20 minutes). Continue baking until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 160°F — total bake time was approximately 2 hours 30 minutes for this large batch. Tent with foil if tops are browning too fast.

steps.title: Brush with maple syrup
steps.text: Immediately out of the oven, generously brush {i12} over the top of each hot loaf — approximately a half cup per loaf. Use the best quality Grade A maple syrup you can find.

steps.title: Finish with flaky salt
steps.text: While the maple syrup is still wet, sprinkle {i13} over the top of each loaf.

steps.title: Cool, slice, and store
steps.text: Allow loaves to cool before slicing. Any extras can be wrapped tightly and frozen; thaw at room temperature. Author notes frozen-then-thawed loaves may be even more moist.

rawText:
CAPTION (as written by the author -- trust these amounts):
If you don’t know about @theselena_v ’s Banana Bread recipe….. now you do. I will shout this recipe from the rooftops. 

This banana bread recipe does make an obscene amount of banana bread but it’s well worth the investment into some XL loaf pans. The butter and buttermilk bring crazy moisture along with the added molasses for flavor….. it’s a stellar recipe. 

One note: I think I probably ended up baking these for about 2 hours and 30 minutes….. Theres a lot of batter there. Keep an eye on your loaves around 90 minutes and go from there until the interior reaches 160 degrees. Also, next time, I think I might increase the amount of salt to further bring out the banana flavor…. Food for thought. 

Straight out of the oven start brushing on that GRADE A maple syrup. You want to splurge on the best maple syrup you can find. If nothing else, to honor the patience and hard work you put in to making these loaves. 

I highly recommend giving this recipe a try. If you have extras, go ahead and wrap them up to freeze and thaw at room temp…. I have never had extras but apparently thawing them from frozen makes them even more moist…… 

Peace and love, 
Madison
